title: DaVita Statement on Xenotransplantation Milestone
summary: DaVita celebrates today's announcement from eGenesis that a patient reached the one-year survival mark after receiving a genetically engineered pig kidney transplant. It's an encouraging milestone...
body_markdown:
DENVER


, Nov. 23, 2026


/PRNewswire/ — DaVita celebrates[today’s announcement from eGenesis](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4829373-1&h=1209298085&u=https%3A%2F%2Fegenesisbio.com%2Fnews-media%2Fpress-releases%2Fegenesis-and-mass-general-brigham-announce-first-patient-to-surpass-one-year-of-dialysis-independence-following-porcine-kidney-transplant&a=today%27s+announcement+from+eGenesis) that a patient reached the one-year survival mark after receiving a genetically engineered pig kidney transplant. It’s an encouraging milestone for the patient and for the field of xenotransplantation.


We’re fierce advocates for advances that help people with kidney disease live longer and live better. Expanding the supply of transplantable organs could give more patients an opportunity they do not have today. That potential is why we’ve long invested in this field, including in eGenesis.


For patients and families wondering what this means for them, it’s too early to know when xenotransplantation could become broadly available. Studies such as eGenesis’s FDA-cleared Phase 1/2/3 clinical trial will help researchers better understand the risks and benefits and how well these kidneys function over time. As with any breakthrough therapeutic approach, building on this progress to make xenotransplantation available to more patients will take time and require several important steps, including regulatory approval, a reliable organ supply, transplant-center capacity, and insurance coverage and reimbursement.


Our commitment is to support progress that expands patients’ options and help patients and families understand what emerging evidence could mean for their care. There is more to learn, but the possibility of helping more people receive a kidney transplant is worth pursuing.
